requirements.summary: The service was active with the requested executable as ExecStart, and both systemd configuration and the live process identity showed inventory-worker. The same state recovered after reboot.

requirements.requirement: Allow the worker up to 30 seconds to finish cleanly when the service stops.
requirements.summary: The effective stop timeout was 30 seconds. A bounded live stop completed successfully within the limit, produced the expected graceful marker, and the service was restored. The reboot shutdown independently produced the marker and the service recovered.

overall_summary: Both material task outcomes are directly demonstrated. The mandatory node-restart protocol is also complete: a healthy pre-restart state and boot identity were captured, restart scheduling was acknowledged, the connection dropped during reboot, the boot identity changed, and the enabled service, runtime user, executable, timeout, and graceful marker recovered. The fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the restart.
limitations: The lifecycle snapshots do not inventory /var/tmp, service-unit contents, local accounts, or the worker executable, so those conclusions depend on the executor command evidence.
No cleanup of /var/tmp/inventory-worker.boot-id.before was captured after the final verification.

operational_hygiene.summary: The account, repaired executable, unit file, service lifecycle operations, and reboot were causally connected to implementation, behavioral verification, or the mandatory restart protocol. The executable repair was justified by direct discovery that the prepared file was malformed and non-executable. No unnecessary troubleshooting mutations were identified. One minor retained artifact remained: /var/tmp/inventory-worker.boot-id.before was created for restart correlation and was still read by the final command, with no subsequent cleanup captured. No failed services, new listeners, package damage, or abandoned /tmp files were observed after execution.
